profiles.meeting_scenario: A state preparedness office is preparing a cross-agency briefing packet for an upcoming hurricane-season tabletop exercise that will use social-network indicators to estimate coordination readiness across state emergency services, state law enforcement, and selected local agencies. The meeting is a coordination check-in between the analyst assembling the statewide readiness materials and the regional law-enforcement coordinator supplying local network inputs. The agenda is to align on which network artifact will go into the briefing packet, confirm what counts as county coverage, coordinate the handoff of updated relationship/contact information, and agree on when the readiness snapshot is considered final. The expected outcome is a shared plan for what each person will deliver by the end of the week so the statewide exercise packet can be assembled without reopening methodology discussions.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: Preparedness metrics, interagency survey analysis, social network mapping for emergency coordination
members.background: Priya works in the state emergency management agency's planning division and has spent the last three years translating survey and exercise data into briefing products for senior leadership.
members.private_state: She wants to lock the briefing inputs quickly so the statewide packet can go to leadership review on schedule, and she is trying to avoid another round of data cleaning after the reporting cut-off.
hidden_assumptions: A 'readiness snapshot' is the frozen baseline used for the exercise packet, based on the latest validated survey extract rather than live updates after the cut-off.
When people refer to 'the March network map,' they mean the cleaned statewide graph generated from the March 18 data freeze in the analytics workspace.

A county is 'covered' once at least one verified agency node from that county appears in the network dataset, because the statewide briefing is about geographic visibility rather than full local representation.
An 'updated contact list' for coordination means official primary and alternate points of contact maintained in WebEOC-compatible format, not informal relationship ties.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.expertise: Multi-agency coordination, county liaison networks, public-safety communications and mutual-aid relationships
members.background: Daniel supports coordination across sheriffs' offices, municipal police departments, and regional emergency managers, and he routinely maintains working relationship maps used during storms and special events.
members.private_state: He wants the state packet to reflect the real operational network in his region, including informal liaison ties that matter in fast-moving incidents, and he is trying to keep local partners from being marked as underprepared because of thin formal survey data.
hidden_assumptions: A 'readiness snapshot' is the near-current operational picture that should include any meaningful updates received before the exercise begins, even if they arrive after an earlier analytic cut-off.
When people mention 'the March network map,' they mean the map shown at the March regional coordination meeting, which included locally maintained ties not yet merged into the statewide cleaned file.
A county is only truly 'covered' when the key coordination actors for that county are represented across the main response functions, not just by one agency node.

An 'updated contact list' includes the unofficial but relied-upon liaison links, mutual-aid group admins, and cross-agency connectors that people actually use during activation, even if they are not formal points of contact.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to finalize the 'readiness snapshot' for the exercise packet this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a fixed baseline generated from the latest validated survey extract and frozen for briefing purposes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the operationally current picture that can still absorb late relationship and contact updates before the exercise starts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In preparedness work, 'snapshot' sounds mutually obvious and neither person expects the other to be talking about a fundamentally different temporal frame because both are focused on the same exercise.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using 'the March map' as the common network visual.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the statewide graph exported from the March 18 cleaned data freeze in her analytics folder.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the regional slide deck map presented in March that already incorporated local liaison ties and mutual-aid links.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts were produced in March, discussed in overlapping meetings, and visually similar enough that the phrase 'the March map' feels sufficiently specific in casual coordination talk.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that several counties are now 'covered' for the packet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 counts a county as covered if at least one verified agency from that county appears in the statewide dataset.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 counts a county as covered only if the county has representation from the main cross-agency coordination actors needed in a real activation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Coverage is a routine status word in coordination meetings, and both standards sound reasonable enough that surface agreement on county names masks the deeper difference in what qualifies.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the contact list update
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Daniel will send Priya the 'updated contact list' for the remaining counties.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a formal list of primary and alternate agency contacts in the state template, suitable for direct upload and validation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to send a broader coordination sheet that includes unofficial connectors, task-force leads, and trusted cross-agency intermediaries alongside official contacts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see contact information as a straightforward handoff item, so neither feels a need to unpack whether the list is an administrative roster or a richer operational network artifact.

For me, the readiness snapshot is the frozen baseline from the latest validated survey extract, and I do not want anything after the reporting cut-off forcing data cleaning again. If Daniel confirms his final handoffs this week, I can keep leadership review on schedule.

To me, a readiness snapshot should reflect the near-current operational picture before the exercise starts, not just an earlier administrative cut. I especially want to get in the relationship updates that keep my counties from looking thinner than they really are.
turns.utterance: That works on my end. I do have a few late updates that should help the readiness snapshot better reflect what's happening on the ground, so this week is actually a good window.
